    retry: { max: 3, backoff: 2s, factor: 2, max_backoff: 30s }

fields.example:
blueprint: health
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  fetch:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [wget, -qO-, "http://localhost:8080/health"] }
    retry: { max: 3, backoff: 2s, factor: 2, max_backoff: 30s }
fields.help: The action the step runs, by its name, with what it is handed under `with`: what most steps are.
fields.name: do

fields.example:
blueprint: order-news
permissions: [blueprints:run]

steps:
  watch:
    call: std/watch
    with: { channel: general, collection: orders }
fields.help: Run another blueprint as a child and wait for its steps. Its outputs become this step's.
fields.name: call

fields.example:
blueprint: order-news
permissions: [blueprints:run]

steps:
  watch:
    spawn: std/watch
    as: order-watch
    with: { channel: general, collection: orders }
fields.help: Start another blueprint as a child and carry on, for something that is to go on beside this one.
fields.name: spawn

fields.example:
blueprint: release
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  build:
    description: Everything it takes to have something to ship.
    task:
      compile: { do: shell, with: { cmd: [make] } }
      test: { do: shell, with: { cmd: [make, test] } }
    retry: 1
    timeout: 30m
fields.help: Run the steps under it as one: if one fails the rest do not run and the task has failed. What is said beside it (`when`, `retry`, `timeout`, `on_fail`) is said once, for all of them.
fields.name: task

fields.example:
blueprint: health
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  fetch:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [wget, -qO-, "http://localhost:8080/health"] }
    retry: { max: 3, backoff: 2s, factor: 2, max_backoff: 30s }
fields.help: What the action named beside it is handed, or the params the blueprint named beside it is started with: each by its name.
fields.name: with

fields.example:
blueprint: deploy
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  build:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make] }

  lint:
    needs: []
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make, lint] }

  ship:
    needs: [build, lint]
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make, ship] }
fields.help: Steps that must settle first. Without it a step follows the one above it; `[]` starts at once.
fields.name: needs

fields.example:
blueprint: deploy
permissions: [shell]

params:
  ship: false

steps:
  ship:
    when: ${params.ship}
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make, ship] }
fields.help: A guard. When false the step is skipped, and what follows still runs.
fields.name: when

fields.after: a length of time, such as 30s or 5m
fields.example:
blueprint: tests
permissions: [shell, channels:write]

steps:
  test:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make, test] }
    timeout: 10m
    on_timeout:
      - do: channel.post
        with: { channel: ops, body: The tests ran for ten minutes and were stopped. }
fields.help: Fail the step if it runs longer, so that one that hangs does not hold the run up.
fields.name: timeout

fields.example:
blueprint: health
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  fetch:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [wget, -qO-, "http://localhost:8080/health"] }
    retry: { max: 3, backoff: 2s, factor: 2, max_backoff: 30s }
fields.help: Try again after a failure: a count, or `max`, `backoff` and `factor`. For a step that may fail for a moment, such as one that asks something over the network.
fields.name: retry

fields.example:
blueprint: tidy
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  lint:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make, lint] }
    allow_failure: true

  said:
    do: log
    with: { message: "The lint went well: ${steps.lint.ok}" }
fields.help: A failure here does not fail the run; later steps see `steps.<id>.failed`.
fields.name: allow_failure

fields.example:
blueprint: build
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  build:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make] }
    again: true
fields.help: Run the step again from its start where the daemon was stopped in the middle of it, in place of failing it as not safe to repeat: for a command that does no harm done twice, such as a build or a test. A failure of its own is not tried again; that is `retry`.
fields.name: again

fields.after: a list, each a watch rule
fields.help: Rules looked at while the step is still running: after so long, every so often, or when a line it prints matches.
fields.name: watch

fields.help: Done as the step starts, before its own action begins.
fields.name: on_start

fields.help: Done when the step has gone well, with `self` the step it belongs to.
fields.name: on_success

fields.help: Done when the step has ended, however it went, after `on_success`, `on_fail` or `on_timeout`; `self.status` says which.
fields.name: on_finish

fields.help: Done when the step fails. It may decide what happens next: `retry`, `continue` or `fail`.
fields.name: on_fail

fields.example:
blueprint: tests
permissions: [shell, channels:write]

steps:
  test:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make, test] }
    timeout: 10m
    on_timeout:
      - do: channel.post
        with: { channel: ops, body: The tests ran for ten minutes and were stopped. }
fields.help: Done when the step runs out of time, in place of `on_fail`. It may decide what happens next.
fields.name: on_timeout

fields.help: Run on another device, through the gateway: for work that has to be done where something is.
fields.name: device

fields.example:
blueprint: build
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  build:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make] }
    measure: build
fields.help: Also report how long the step took under this name, to be looked at beside every other time it ran.
fields.name: measure

fields.help: For `call`, `spawn` and `task`: names and values that everything measured under the step carries, as in `{ experiment: cart, variant: a }`, so that two ways of doing the same work can be told apart and compared.
fields.name: labels

fields.example:
blueprint: order-news
permissions: [blueprints:run]

steps:
  watch:
    spawn: std/watch
    as: order-watch
    with: { channel: general, collection: orders }
fields.help: For `call` and `spawn`: the child's name within its parent, by which it is found again when the blueprint is applied again.
fields.name: as

fields.help: For `call` and `spawn`, where the blueprint runs under none of its project's environments: the one its child is started under, as `prod`, held there to that environment's rules (who approves what goes under it, which branches it lets run). Under one, a child is under that one and no other.
fields.name: environment

fields.example:
blueprint: build
permissions: [shell, agents:write]

steps:
  build:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make] }
    if_fail_ask_agent: builder
    else: build-broken
fields.help: When the step fails, tell this agent what failed and let it put it right; it says whether the step is run again.
fields.name: if_fail_ask_agent

fields.example:
blueprint: build
permissions: [shell, agents:write]

steps:
  build:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make] }
    if_fail_ask_agent: builder
    else: build-broken
fields.help: With `if_fail_ask_agent`: the name the step fails under when the agent could not put it right.
fields.name: else

fields.example:
blueprint: greet-each

params:
  names: [ada, grace]

steps:
  greet:
    for_each: ${params.names}
    do: log
    with: { message: "Hello, ${item}, number ${index}." }
fields.help: Run once for each element of a list, in order, or so many times where it is handed a number (`item` then goes from 1 to it); `item` and `index` are available.
fields.name: for_each

fields.example:
blueprint: release
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  build:
    description: Everything it takes to have something to ship.
    task:
      compile: { do: shell, with: { cmd: [make] } }
      test: { do: shell, with: { cmd: [make, test] } }
    retry: 1
    timeout: 30m
fields.help: What the step is for, in a sentence. Shown for the step in the node view and in the steps of a run.
fields.name: description

fields.example:
blueprint: build
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  build:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make] }
    env: { RELEASE: "1" }
fields.help: Environment for the action, added to the blueprint's: each variable text, or a secret's name as `{ secret: <name> }`.
fields.name: env

shapes.help: One thing a blueprint does: an action, another blueprint called or started, or a task of steps, with what is said around it: when it runs, what it waits for, how long it may take and what happens if it fails.
shapes.name: step

shapes.example:
blueprint: health
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  fetch:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [wget, -qO-, "http://localhost:8080/health"] }
    retry: { max: 3, backoff: 2s, factor: 2, max_backoff: 30s }

fields.example:
blueprint: health
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  fetch:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [wget, -qO-, "http://localhost:8080/health"] }
    retry: { max: 3, backoff: 2s, factor: 2, max_backoff: 30s }
fields.help: How many times to try again after the first.
fields.name: max

fields.after: a length of time, such as 30s or 5m
fields.example:
blueprint: health
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  fetch:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [wget, -qO-, "http://localhost:8080/health"] }
    retry: { max: 3, backoff: 2s, factor: 2, max_backoff: 30s }
fields.help: How long to wait before trying again. 1s unless said.
fields.name: backoff

fields.example:
blueprint: health
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  fetch:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [wget, -qO-, "http://localhost:8080/health"] }
    retry: { max: 3, backoff: 2s, factor: 2, max_backoff: 30s }
fields.help: What each wait is multiplied by to make the next. 2 unless said.
fields.name: factor

fields.after: a length of time, such as 30s or 5m
fields.example:
blueprint: health
permissions: [shell]

steps:
  fetch:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [wget, -qO-, "http://localhost:8080/health"] }
    retry: { max: 3, backoff: 2s, factor: 2, max_backoff: 30s }
fields.help: The longest a wait may grow to. 5m unless said.
fields.name: max_backoff

shapes.help: How a step that failed is tried again: a count alone, or how many times and how long to wait before each, the wait growing each time.
shapes.name: retry

fields.help: The action done at that point, by its name, with what it is handed under `with`.
fields.name: do

fields.help: Say an event when this is done: short for `do: emit`, with its topic and what it carries.
fields.name: emit

fields.help: What the action named beside it is handed, or the params the blueprint named beside it is started with: each by its name.
fields.name: with

fields.example:
blueprint: build
permissions: [shell, channels:write]

params:
  tell: true

steps:
  build:
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [make] }
    on_success:
      - when: ${params.tell}
        do: channel.post
        with: { channel: ops, body: Built. }
fields.help: Only when this holds is the hook done; it is passed over otherwise.
fields.name: when

shapes.help: Something done at a point in the life of a step or of the blueprint (as it starts, goes well, fails, ends or is stopped): an action, or an event said. Written as the action's name alone where it needs nothing.
shapes.name: hook

fields.help: Run an action, or decide what happens to the step: `retry`, `continue` or `fail`.
fields.name: do

fields.help: Say an event when this is done: short for `do: emit`, with its topic and what it carries.
fields.name: emit

fields.help: What the action named beside it is handed, or the params the blueprint named beside it is started with: each by its name.
fields.name: with

fields.help: Only when this holds is it done or decided, as `self.attempts` says how often the step was tried.
fields.name: when

shapes.help: Something done when a step has failed or run out of time, which may also decide what becomes of the step: tried again (`retry`), let pass (`continue`) or failed (`fail`).
shapes.name: failure_hook

fields.after: a length of time, such as 30s or 5m
fields.help: Once, when the step has run this long. Written with `${ }` it is worked out as the step begins, and where it comes to nothing the rule is never timed.
fields.name: after

fields.after: a length of time, such as 30s or 5m
fields.help: Again and again, this far apart, while the step runs: worked out as the step begins where it is written with `${ }`, and never timed where that comes to nothing.
fields.name: every

fields.help: When a line the step prints matches this pattern, once per attempt.
fields.name: log

fields.help: The action done when the rule fires, with what it is handed under `with`.
fields.name: do

fields.help: Say an event when this is done: short for `do: emit`, with its topic and what it carries.
fields.name: emit

fields.help: What the action named beside it is handed, or the params the blueprint named beside it is started with: each by its name.
fields.name: with

fields.help: Only when this holds does the rule fire.
fields.name: when

fields.help: Also stop the step, as failed.
fields.name: fail

shapes.help: A rule looked at while a step is still running: after so long, every so often, or when a line the step prints matches, something is done, and the step may be stopped as failed.
shapes.name: watch

shapes.example:
blueprint: shipped-news
permissions: [channels:write]

on:
  shipped:
    event: order.shipped
    outside: true
    when: ${ event.data.to != "" }
    do: channel.post
    with: { channel: general, body: "Order ${event.data.order} is on its way to ${event.data.to}." }

fields.example:
blueprint: shipped-news
permissions: [channels:write]

on:
  shipped:
    event: order.shipped
    outside: true
    when: ${ event.data.to != "" }
    do: channel.post
    with: { channel: general, body: "Order ${event.data.order} is on its way to ${event.data.to}." }
fields.help: Fires on an event whose topic matches. `*` is one word, `**` any number.
fields.name: event

fields.after: a length of time, such as 30s or 5m
fields.example:
blueprint: hourly-copy
permissions: [shell]

on:
  hourly:
    every: 1h
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [cp, data.db, backup/data.db] }
fields.help: Fires on a timer, this far apart: for what is done again and again while the instance is alive.
fields.name: every

fields.example:
blueprint: copy-before-dawn
description: Copy the database somewhere safe at half past two each night, by the clock in Zagreb.
permissions: [shell]

on:
  copied:
    at: 02:30 Europe/Zagreb
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [cp, data.db, backup/data.db] }
fields.help: Fires at a time of day in the zone written after it, `02:00 Europe/Zagreb`, with the days before it where it is not every day (`mon,thu 09:30 UTC`). A time that came while the factory was stopped is fired once, as it is back.
fields.name: at

fields.example:
blueprint: code-moved
permissions: [shell]

on:
  moved:
    poll: { every: 1m, do: shell, with: { cmd: [git, rev-parse, HEAD] } }
    do: emit
    with: { topic: code.moved, head: "${event.data.stdout}" }
fields.help: Fires when an action's result changes. For things that cannot say when they change.
fields.name: poll

fields.example:
blueprint: one-order

params:
  order: { type: string, description: The order to follow. }

state:
  where: ""

on:
  shipped:
    event: order.shipped
    outside: true
    for: { order: "${params.order}" }
    do: set
    with: { where: "${event.data.to}" }
fields.help: Which events are addressed to it: fields of the event's data and the value each must have, as in `{ id: "${params.item}" }`, a field inside one named by its path (`fields.sprint`). The conductor decides that, so a handler is not woken for what is another's.
fields.name: for

fields.example:
blueprint: shipped-news
permissions: [channels:write]

on:
  shipped:
    event: order.shipped
    outside: true
    when: ${ event.data.to != "" }
    do: channel.post
    with: { channel: general, body: "Order ${event.data.order} is on its way to ${event.data.to}." }
fields.help: A guard over `event`: the handler runs only for an event of which it holds.
fields.name: when

fields.example:
blueprint: every-failure
permissions: [channels:write]

on:
  failed:
    event: run.failed
    scope: fleet
    do: channel.post
    with: { channel: ops, body: "${event.data.blueprint} failed: ${event.data.error}" }
fields.help: Whose events it hears: its own project's unless said, or every project's, or only those of what it started.
fields.name: scope

of.help: events of its own project and the factory's own, which are no project's (the default)
of.name: project

of.help: every event in the factory, whichever project's
of.name: fleet

of.help: only events from this instance and its children
of.name: own

of.help: only events from the instance this one is attached to
of.name: target

fields.after: a length of time, such as 30s or 5m
fields.example:
blueprint: burst-news

on:
  changed:
    event: record.updated
    debounce: 10s
    do: emit
    with: { topic: news.changed, record: "${event.data.id}" }
fields.help: Makes a burst of events one run, with the latest of them.
fields.name: debounce

fields.example:
blueprint: lock
one_at_a_time: true

state:
  holder: ""

on:
  take:
    event: lock.take
    outside: true
    when: ${ state.holder == "" }
    do: set
    with: { holder: "${event.data.who}" }

  give:
    event: lock.give
    outside: true
    do: set
    with: { holder: "" }
fields.help: Its event is said from outside: by a person, a key or a caller, and by no blueprint. The check then does not look for a blueprint that says it.
fields.name: outside

fields.example:
blueprint: orders
permissions: [shell]

on:
  paid:
    event: order.paid
    outside: true
    turn: "${event.data.order}"
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [./pack, "${event.data.order}"] }
fields.help: What its events take turns by, worked out from each as it comes: `turn: "${event.data.id}"`. What comes to the same key, here or at another handler of this instance that says `turn`, is handled one at a time, and what one handler hears of it in the order it was said; what comes to another key is handled beside it. For an instance that looks after many things of a kind, so that one of them holds up none of the others.
fields.name: turn

fields.example:
blueprint: shipped-news
permissions: [channels:write]

on:
  shipped:
    event: order.shipped
    outside: true
    steps:
      said:
        do: channel.post
        with: { channel: general, body: "Order ${event.data.order} is on its way." }

      kept:
        do: emit
        with: { topic: news.said, order: "${event.data.order}" }
fields.help: What to do, as a graph of steps, where it is more than one thing.
fields.name: steps

fields.example:
blueprint: hourly-copy
permissions: [shell]

on:
  hourly:
    every: 1h
    do: shell
    with: { cmd: [cp, data.db, backup/data.db] }
fields.help: What to do, when it is one action.
fields.name: do

fields.example:
blueprint: copy-on-asking
permissions: [blueprints:run]

on:
  asked:
    event: copy.asked
    outside: true
    call: std/snapshot
    with: { to: "${event.data.to}" }
fields.help: What to do, when it is one blueprint.
fields.name: call

fields.example:
blueprint: copy-on-asking
permissions: [blueprints:run]

on:
  asked:
    event: copy.asked
    outside: true
    call: std/snapshot
    with: { to: "${event.data.to}" }
fields.help: What the action named beside it is handed, or the params the blueprint named beside it is started with: each by its name.
fields.name: with

shapes.help: What an instance does each time something happens while it is alive: an event it hears, a timer, or an answer that changes, and the steps it runs then. Written under `on`, each by a name of your own.
shapes.name: handler

shapes.example:
blueprint: code-moved
permissions: [shell]

on:
  moved:
    poll: { every: 1m, do: shell, with: { cmd: [git, rev-parse, HEAD] } }
    do: emit
    with: { topic: code.moved, head: "${event.data.stdout}" }

fields.after: a length of time, such as 30s or 5m
fields.example:
blueprint: code-moved
permissions: [shell]

on:
  moved:
    poll: { every: 1m, do: shell, with: { cmd: [git, rev-parse, HEAD] } }
    do: emit
    with: { topic: code.moved, head: "${event.data.stdout}" }
fields.help: How often to ask, after the first time, which is as the handler begins to listen. Never more often than every 5s.
fields.name: every

fields.example:
blueprint: code-moved
permissions: [shell]

on:
  moved:
    poll: { every: 1m, do: shell, with: { cmd: [git, rev-parse, HEAD] } }
    do: emit
    with: { topic: code.moved, head: "${event.data.stdout}" }
fields.help: The action whose result is watched.
fields.name: do

fields.example:
blueprint: code-moved
permissions: [shell]

on:
  moved:
    poll: { every: 1m, do: shell, with: { cmd: [git, rev-parse, HEAD] } }
    do: emit
    with: { topic: code.moved, head: "${event.data.stdout}" }
fields.help: What the action named beside it is handed, or the params the blueprint named beside it is started with: each by its name.
fields.name: with

shapes.help: What a handler asks again and again of something that cannot say when it changes: an action and how often, the handler running each time the answer is other than the time before. It is first asked as the handler begins to listen, and that answer is only what the next is told from.
shapes.name: poll

step.help: true when it finished without failing
step.name: ok

step.help: how it went, as a word
step.name: status

step.help: how many things that is, where it is a list: one for each element of a `for_each`
step.name: count

step.help: why it failed, when it did
step.name: error

step.help: why it failed, alone: what the innermost step said, without the steps it came up through
step.name: reason

step.help: how many times it was tried
step.name: attempts
